_comment: The one place BGL categories are defined. Prompts, eval, routing and the UI all read this file. Codes are the label tokens at the start of each BGL.log line ('-' = normal). KERNPROG is mapped to normal on purpose: its only message, 'program interrupt', appears 3,662 times labelled normal and 5 times labelled KERNPROG, so no model can learn it (see PLAN.md, BGL finding 3).

categories.name: normal
categories.definition: Routine operation, including noisy FATAL/ERROR-level messages that are not real alerts (core dumps being generated, ido ASSERT noise, register dumps, node card status reports).

categories.name: memory / CPU fault
categories.definition: A compute node hit a processor or memory hardware fault: TLB error interrupt, data storage interrupt, machine check, floating point unavailable, DDR bit steering failure.

categories.name: kernel crash / panic
categories.definition: The compute node kernel stopped: kernel panic, rts panic, kernel terminated, rts assertion failed, microloader assertion.

categories.name: I/O node connection lost
categories.definition: The I/O daemon (ciod) lost its socket connection to a compute node: link severed, connection reset, connection timed out, failed to read message prefix, or bad packets on the tree network.

categories.name: filesystem mount failure
categories.definition: A node could not mount or use its filesystem: Lustre mount FAILED, unable to mount filesystem, or Input/output error when changing into a job directory.

categories.name: job launch / resource failure
categories.definition: A job could not start because ciod failed to create the node map: resource temporarily unavailable, device busy, no child processes, cannot allocate memory.

categories.name: link / network hardware
categories.definition: Interconnect hardware failed: midplane switch link card errors (iap/pap/bll failed, port disconnected), no ethernet link, uncorrectable torus error, external input interrupt.

categories.name: power and control system
categories.definition: Power or service/control infrastructure failed: power deactivated, power good signal lost, power module fault, mailbox or idoproxy socket closed or connection lost, control daemons (mmcs_server, ciodb) exited, monitor exceptions.
